stem: Plants along one room edge are shorter with longer internodes than plants in the center. What is the best first record?
choices: Record that edge plants have poor genetics because the pattern is concentrated along the room perimeter.
Recommend a room-wide lighting redesign because longer internodes indicate insufficient light.
Remove the edge plants before documenting them so only normal crop structure remains in the comparison.
Record the edge-concentrated pattern with representative measurements and available light, environment, irrigation, and plant-history context before assigning cause.
rationale: The spatial concentration is the most important first finding. Representative plant measurements and nearby environmental/process context make the pattern reconstructable and give later reviewers evidence to compare possible light, environment, irrigation, or plant-history explanations. Calling genetics or lighting the cause before that comparison goes beyond what the observation establishes.
